analysis.one_liner: Adani Energy Solutions runs India's largest private power transmission network, the Mumbai electricity distribution business (AEML), a fast-growing smart-metering arm, and a newer EPC-style "Energy Solutions Platform".
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on 22 October 2026 (three days from now) to approve Q2/H1 FY27 results, with an investor call on 23 October; the trading window has been closed since 1 October. On 6 October 2026 the company signed an agreement to buy 100% of Satara Power Transmission from PFC Consulting, and it is also set to win Bihar's first intrastate transmission scheme under competitive bidding. The stock has fallen 21% in the last three months (versus -5.6% for Nifty and -12.9% for peer Power Grid), giving back a chunk of its 1-year gain heading into results.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of this company as three businesses stapled together: wires that move power across states (transmission, the biggest and steadiest earner), the company that supplies electricity to Mumbai households (distribution), and a newer, fast-scaling unit that installs smart meters and does EPC-type contract work. The tension is that the newer, lower-margin businesses are growing so fast they are diluting the overall profit margin even as total profit rises - and all of this expansion is being funded with rising debt. Revenue and EBITDA are genuinely growing, but you are paying a rich valuation for a leveraged, capex-heavy growth story, not a mature, cash-generative utility.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter): revenue from operations up ~42% YoY to roughly ₹9,700 crore, EBITDA up 58% to a record ₹3,178 crore - but press reports put PAT at anywhere from ₹1,149 crore to ₹1,237 crore depending on the source, so treat the exact figure as approximate until checked on the exchange filing. Importantly, core operating EBITDA margin (ex other income) fell to 30.98% from 33.94% a year earlier - revenue grew faster than profit because the mix shifted toward the lower-margin Energy Solutions Platform, whose revenue jumped from about ₹18 crore to ₹1,839 crore. The September 2025 quarter (Q2 FY26) showed PAT falling ~21-28% YoY to ₹534-557 crore - but that drop is an accounting artifact: the year-ago quarter had benefited from a one-off ₹314 crore deferred-tax gain, so the YoY comparison overstates any real deterioration. For FY26 as a whole, reported PAT of ₹2,393 crore looked like a 160% jump, but that headline number is almost entirely explained by FY25 carrying a one-off ₹1,506 crore exceptional loss from the Dahanu Thermal Power Plant divestment; stripping that out, underlying PAT growth was closer to 32%, with record EBITDA of ₹8,726 crore (+13% YoY).
analysis.performance_read: The stock trades at ₹1,364.9, still 66.8% below its September 2022 peak of ₹4,105.4 - and there is no split, bonus or demerger in the data to explain that gap away, so it reflects a genuine market de-rating (coinciding with the broader Adani-group scrutiny that began in early 2023) rather than a corporate-action artifact. Over 1 year the stock has sharply outperformed, up 45.7% versus Nifty's -11.4% and peer Power Grid's -10.3%. But zoom out to 5 years and the picture flips uncomfortably: the stock is down 21.8% while Power Grid is up 114.6% and Nifty is up 24.3% - someone who bought this stock five years ago has lost money while the sector benchmark more than doubled. The last 3 months (-21.1% vs Nifty -5.6%) show the recent rally partly unwinding just ahead of results.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 57x and P/B of about 6.6x, the stock trades well above typical power-sector multiples (including peer Power Grid). That premium exists because the market is pricing in a multi-year transmission capex pipeline, the smart-metering rollout, and the newly scaling Energy Solutions Platform - growth that hasn't yet fully shown up in trailing earnings. Whether that premium is justified depends entirely on whether execution continues at the current pace; on trailing earnings alone, it is expensive, not cheap.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is volume-led, not margin-led: Q1 FY27 revenue grew faster (42-54% YoY) than core EBITDA margin could keep pace with, because the fastest-growing piece - the Energy Solutions Platform - carries a lower margin than the transmission core. That is a reasonable trade in a capex-building phase, but it means investors are buying revenue growth more than margin expansion right now.
analysis.health_read: Cash profit did grow (reportedly up 70% to ₹1,776 crore in Q1 FY27), so profits are broadly converting to cash. But net debt rose to about ₹39,268 crore in FY26 from ₹30,076 crore in FY25, pushing net debt/EBITDA up to roughly 4.5x from 3.2x, with debt-to-equity near 1.9x. The real concern here is financial risk from an aggressive, debt-funded capex program, not operating/business risk - EBITDA and revenue are both growing in a predictable, regulated/contracted business.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter (Adani family/group) holding rose from about 71.2% in January 2026 to 74.3% after on-market purchases between late March and mid-June 2026. Promoter share pledging stands at 0% as of the June 2026 quarter, with all pledges reportedly released - a positive signal given the group's past pledging concerns. FII holding is modest at ~13%, but domestic institutional (DII) holding is essentially negligible at ~0.07%, and there is no well-known independent institutional or value investor visible on the register - domestic mutual fund participation remains almost nil, which likely still reflects institutional caution toward the Adani group rather than pure float constraints.
strengths: Record FY26 EBITDA of ₹8,726 crore, up 13% YoY, with Q1 FY27 EBITDA up 58% YoY to ₹3,178 crore - the highest quarterly EBITDA in the company's history.
Promoter pledge down to 0% as of the June 2026 quarter, removing a key governance overhang that has dogged Adani-group stocks previously.
Mumbai distribution arm (AEML) maintained best-in-class distribution losses of 4.30% in H1 FY26, a genuine operational moat in that business.
Active project pipeline additions - the October 2026 Satara Power Transmission acquisition and the Bihar intrastate transmission win - extend the transmission backlog underpinning future growth.
watchpoints: Net debt/EBITDA climbed to roughly 4.5x in FY26 from 3.2x in FY25, with net debt up to ~₹39,268 crore - leverage is rising faster than cash flow right now.
Core operating EBITDA margin fell to 30.98% in Q1 FY27 from 33.94% a year earlier, as the mix shifted toward lower-margin Energy Solutions Platform revenue.
The stock has fallen 21% in 3 months into the 22 October 2026 results date, more than double the Nifty's decline over the same period.
A P/E near 57x and P/B near 6.6x leave little room for execution slippage on the HVDC ramp-up, smart-meter rollout, or new transmission projects.
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results and management commentary on 22-23 October 2026 - specifically whether the core EBITDA margin stabilizes or recovers from Q1 FY27's 30.98% and whether net debt/EBITDA holds near 4.5x or climbs further, since that resolves whether this is durable, compounding growth or growth bought with margin and balance-sheet strain.
analysis.data_notes: PAT, EBITDA and revenue trends were cross-checked across multiple press sources (Business Standard, Upstox, Angel One, Multibagg, Marketsmojo, Investing.com) and company press releases, and they corroborate the same underlying story (growth diluted by one-off base effects and margin mix-shift). However, exact figures vary across secondary sources - e.g., Q1 FY27 PAT is cited anywhere from ₹1,149 crore to ₹1,237 crore - so treat precise rupee figures as approximate pending verification against the company's exchange filing or Screener. Net debt, debt/equity and ROE/ROCE figures came from secondary aggregators (stockanalysis.com, pocketful, gurufocus) rather than the company balance sheet directly, and showed minor variance across sources (e.g., ROE cited as both 9.40% and 10.08%) - not independently recomputed here. Market cap (~₹1.67 lakh crore) and P/E (~57x) are from a secondary valuation source, not recomputed against the verified last close of ₹1,364.9.
